title: HA tag enables highly efficient detection of heterologous proteins in Phaeodactylum tricornutum exconjugants
author: Jernej Turnšek

steps.title: Harvest cells by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Spin down approximately 1 × 10⁷–1 × 10⁸ Phaeodactylum tricornutum cells for 10 min at 4000 rpm and 10 °C; keep tubes on ice throughout the protocol.

steps.title: Resuspend pellets in lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellets in 50–200 µL of cell lysis buffer containing 50 mM Tris‑HCl, 200 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT and 1 mM PMSF.

steps.title: Sonicate cell lysate
steps.instruction: Sonicate the resuspended lysate using a Bioruptor UCD‑200™ with cycles of 30 s on / 1 min off for a total of 15 min.

steps.title: Separate soluble and insoluble fractions
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate for 45 min at 13 500 rpm and 10 °C. Collect the supernatant (soluble fraction) and resuspend the pellet/insoluble fraction in 100 µL lysis buffer.

steps.title: Prepare running buffer, gel and load samples
steps.instruction: Prepare MOPS running buffer by mixing 665 mL MQ water with 35 mL 20× MOPS buffer. Use NuPAGE 4–12 % Bis‑Tris 1.5 mm gels (10 wells). Add 500 µL NuPAGE Antioxidant to the inner reservoir of the gel tank. Load 10 µL of supernatant (≈10 µg protein) and 10 µL of pellet suspension (≈1 µL stock) together with 6 µL MagicMark protein standard into separate wells.

substeps.instruction: Mix 665 mL MQ + 35 mL 20× MOPS buffer.
Set up NuPAGE 4–12 % Bis‑Tris gel (1.5 mm, 10 wells).
Add 500 µL NuPAGE Antioxidant to inner reservoir.
Load 10 µL supernatant (10 µg protein), 10 µL pellet suspension, and 6 µL MagicMark standard.

steps.title: Prepare wet transfer buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 40 mL NuPAGE Transfer Buffer (20×), 160 mL methanol, 600 mL MQ water and 800 µL NuPAGE Antioxidant to make the wet transfer buffer; use with an XCell II™ Blot Module and PVDF membranes.

steps.title: Prepare sample mixes and denature
steps.instruction: For each 40 µL sample: add 10 µL NuPAGE LDS Sample Buffer (4×) and 4 µL NuPAGE Sample Reducing Agent (10×). For the supernatant mix, add the appropriate amount of protein and MQ to 40 µL total. For the pellet mix, add 4 µL pellet suspension and 22 µL MQ to 40 µL total. Incubate both mixes at 70 °C for 15 min.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 µL LDS Sample Buffer (4×) and 4 µL Reducing Agent (10×) to each tube.
Supernatant: add 40 µg protein and MQ to 40 µL total.
Pellet: add 4 µL pellet suspension and 22 µL MQ to 40 µL total.

steps.title: Activate and equilibrate PVDF membrane
steps.instruction: Activate each PVDF membrane in methanol for ~1 min, then briefly wash in MQ and leave the membrane immersed in transfer buffer; keep the supplied filter papers soaking in transfer buffer while activating membranes.

steps.title: Assemble transfer sandwich and mark orientation
steps.instruction: Dissassemble the gels, stack the gel, PVDF membrane, filter papers and sponges to form the wet transfer sandwich. Cut the top‑right corner of each membrane to indicate the protein‑facing side.

substeps.instruction: Disassemble gels and arrange gel‑membrane‑filter‑sponge sandwich.
Cut top‑right corner of each membrane for orientation tracking.

steps.title: Transfer proteins via wet blot
steps.instruction: Run a wet transfer at 30 V for 1 h using the assembled sandwich.

steps.title: Wash membrane with MQ (first wash)
steps.instruction: Wash each membrane twice with 20 mL MQ for 5 min per wash on a gentle rocking platform (setting 1) at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare blocking buffer
steps.instruction: For two membranes, mix 10 mL MQ, 4 mL Part A and 6 mL Part B to make the blocking solution.

steps.title: Block membrane
steps.instruction: Incubate each membrane with 10 mL blocking buffer for at least 1 h at room temperature; alternatively, block for 2 days at 4 °C followed by ~1 h 15 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash membrane after blocking
steps.instruction: Wash each membrane twice with 20 mL MQ for 5 min per wash on gentle rocking at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare primary antibody dilution
steps.instruction: Make a 1:10 000 dilution of HA‑tag monoclonal antibody by mixing 14 mL MQ, 4 mL Part A, 2 mL Part B and 2 µL antibody stock (total 20 mL).

steps.title: Incubate membrane with primary antibody
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL of the primary antibody solution to each membrane and incubate for approximately 3 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare wash solution
steps.instruction: Prepare 1× wash solution by mixing 150 mL MQ with 10 mL Wash Solution (16×) to obtain 160 mL total.

steps.title: Wash membrane after primary antibody
steps.instruction: Wash each membrane four times with 20 mL wash solution for 5 min per wash on gentle rocking.

steps.title: Incubate membrane with secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Incubate each membrane in 10 mL anti‑mouse secondary antibody solution for 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash membrane after secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Wash each membrane four times with 20 mL wash solution for 5 min per wash on gentle rocking.

steps.title: Final MQ washes
steps.instruction: Wash each membrane three times with 20 mL MQ for 2 min per wash.

steps.title: Apply CDP‑Star substrate
steps.instruction: Remove excess liquid, place the membrane on transparent plastic foil and evenly cover it with 2 mL Novex CDP‑Star alkaline phosphatase substrate.

steps.title: Cover membrane with second plastic sheet
steps.instruction: Remove any remaining liquid and cover the membrane with another transparent plastic sheet.
